classification.difficultyReason: Infer the missing rectangle width from its area and give both possible coordinate configurations.

content.prompt:
The number plane axes have markers at $1\text{ cm}$ intervals; that is, the point $(1,0)$ is $1\text{ cm}$ from the origin etc.

$AB$ is an interval on the number plane. $A$ has coordinates $(0,4)$ and $B$ has coordinates $(0,10)$. Points $C$ and $D$ are such that $ABCD$ is a rectangle of area $42\text{ cm}^2$. Find the possible coordinates of $C$ and $D$.

answer.short:
$C(7,10),\ D(7,4)$ or $C(-7,10),\ D(-7,4)$.

The vertical side is $6\text{ cm}$, so the perpendicular width is $7\text{ cm}$ on either side of the $y$-axis.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=(10-4)\text{ cm}\\AB&=6\text{ cm}\\\text{Width}&=\frac{42}{6}\text{ cm}\\\text{Width}&=7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The other two vertices are $7$ units horizontally from $AB$. Opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel, so $C$ has the same $y$-coordinate as $B$, and $D$ has the same $y$-coordinate as $A$.

To the right: $C(7,10)$ and $D(7,4)$.

To the left: $C(-7,10)$ and $D(-7,4)$.
